What to buy in Porto — and what to skip | Day in Portugal
Port wine, tinned fish, a bar of soap, a tile. What is worth carrying home from Porto, and what is a tourist trap.

Porto · to take home
Four things worth the weight. The rest is a keyring.
Port wine barrels stacked in a Gaia cellar
A bottle from the cellar you actually visited.
Buy it at the end of the tasting, not from a riverside stall with a plastic cork. The lodge shops in Gaia sell every age and size, and most will pack a bottle for the plane.
Choose a cellar in Gaia
Or book the tasting straight away:
Cálem cellar tour and tasting
(Tiqets). Port in a lighter bag: the port-filled chocolates of
Arcádia
, a Porto chocolatier since 1933.
Colourful tins of Portuguese canned fish on shop shelves
Tinned fish
Sardines, mackerel, octopus. Conservas are the honest souvenir. A good grocer in Cedofeita beats the shop with the giant sardine on the door.
See how they are made: Pinhais factory tour
Tiqets · Matosinhos
To buy: the Comur cannery runs the
Fantastic World of the Portuguese Sardine
shops and sells online. Theatrical, but the tins are real.
Claus Porto soaps wrapped in illustrated paper, boxed on a shop shelf
Soap from Claus Porto
If you want something that lasts after the wine is gone. Their own shop is in the centre; the airport also sells it, worse value. They also sell
online
Claus Porto shop on Rua das Flores
For soap plus everything else Portuguese-made in one stop — tins, ceramics, notebooks:
A Vida Portuguesa
, with a shop at Time Out Porto in São Bento station.
A single patterned azulejo tile on a facade in Porto
One tile, not a set.
Azulejos as a single piece travel. A “hand-painted” stack on Rua das Flores is often a mould. Better: paint your own.
Paint a tile: azulejo workshop in Porto
Want one painted by professionals?
Fábrica Sant’Anna
has hand-painted tiles since 1741 — the workshop is in Lisbon, and they sell online.
We do not run a shop. Cork bags, rooster magnets and “I love Porto” shirts are fine if they make you smile — they are not why you came.
